lab_title: The DNA Double Helix and Semiconservative Replication
top_level_objectives: Identify the structural components of the DNA double helix, including the sugar-phosphate backbones and nitrogenous bases
Explain how antiparallel strand orientation arises from 5' to 3' directionality
Apply complementary base-pairing rules (A-T, G-C) and their hydrogen bonding patterns
Describe the roles of helicase, single-strand binding proteins, DNA polymerase, and DNA ligase in replication
Explain why DNA polymerase directionality forces leading vs lagging strand synthesis
Explain and demonstrate the semiconservative nature of DNA replication

scenes.brief_purpose: Orient students to the overall 3D shape of DNA before examining its parts
key_visuals: A large rotating double helix model floating in the AR space
Two ribbon-like backbones spiraling around a shared central axis
Color-coded rungs representing base pairs connecting the backbones
student_actions: Walk around and view the helix from multiple angles
Rotate and scale the model using pinch/drag gestures
Tap on the backbone and base-pair regions to reveal labels

scenes.brief_purpose: Show students how the repeating sugar-phosphate units create a directional strand
key_visuals: Zoomed-in view of a single backbone strand with deoxyribose sugars and phosphate groups linked in sequence
Highlighted 5' carbon and 3' carbon at opposite ends of the strand
Arrow overlay indicating the 5' to 3' direction
student_actions: Trace the sugar-phosphate chain from the 5' end to the 3' end with a finger swipe
Tap the 5' and 3' carbons to display directional labels
Answer a quick check question identifying which end is 5' vs 3'

scenes.brief_purpose: Connect backbone directionality to the antiparallel arrangement and show how bases pair across the helix
key_visuals: Two full strands displayed side by side, one running 5' to 3' and the other 3' to 5'
Nitrogenous bases (A, T, G, C) projecting inward and pairing across the helix interior
Dashed lines representing hydrogen bonds: two between A-T, three between G-C
student_actions: Drag individual bases to match them with their correct complementary partner
Count and confirm the number of hydrogen bonds for an A-T pair versus a G-C pair
Toggle a view that highlights the antiparallel orientation of the two backbones

scenes.scene_name: Opening the Helix: Helicase and SSBs
scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the initiation of replication and the proteins that unwind and stabilize the DNA
key_visuals: A replication fork forming as helicase unwinds the double helix
Single-strand binding proteins attaching to the separated strands to prevent re-annealing
Split view showing the parental strands opening into a Y-shaped fork
student_actions: Tap helicase to trigger an animation of strand unwinding
Place single-strand binding proteins onto the exposed single strands
Observe and describe in a short prompt why the strands need to be stabilized

scenes.scene_name: DNA Polymerase and the Leading Strand
scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate continuous synthesis on the leading strand and reinforce the 5' to 3' synthesis constraint
key_visuals: DNA polymerase bound to the leading strand template, synthesizing continuously toward the fork
Newly formed nucleotides being added in the 5' to 3' direction
Directional arrows showing the new strand growing in the same direction as fork movement
student_actions: Guide DNA polymerase along the leading strand template by dragging it toward the fork
Select correct incoming nucleotides based on the template base
Answer a prompt explaining why synthesis is continuous on this strand

scenes.brief_purpose: Show why the antiparallel structure forces discontinuous synthesis on the other template strand
key_visuals: DNA polymerase synthesizing short Okazaki fragments away from the replication fork
Multiple fragment segments appearing sequentially along the lagging strand template
DNA ligase animation sealing the gaps between fragments
student_actions: Assemble Okazaki fragments in the correct order by tapping template segments
Trigger DNA ligase to join adjacent fragments
Compare leading vs lagging strand synthesis using a side-by-side toggle

scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate understanding that each daughter molecule contains one parental and one new strand
key_visuals: Two completed daughter DNA double helices displayed side by side
Color-coded strands: original parental strand in one color, newly synthesized strand in another
Split-screen comparison of the original parent molecule versus the two daughter molecules
student_actions: Color-label each strand in the daughter molecules as 'parental' or 'new'
Drag daughter molecules apart to confirm each contains one strand of each type
Complete a final summary quiz question describing semiconservative replication in their own words
